evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2019 (7 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2018 (fire R21721), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
W facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 20 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

R6F-grouse-walk-0002.parkWhat: pull off on Tahtsa FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Trail: Sibola Snowmobile Trails, 4.8 km stretch.
100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
3 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
6 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.

flags.t: MU (Management Unit) 6-9, Region 6 Skeena. Near the MU line: check the MU map.

seasonRows.notes: No row in the Region 6 table (pages 50 and 51), so no general open season (page 5: open seasons are only those in the synopsis).

plan: Drive: from Village of Burns Lake, about 144 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Tibbets Creek Rd, Hwy 16, Hwy 35, Brown Rd.

R6F-grouse-walk-0002.recDirections: From Hwy 16 near Houston, turn onto Morice River FSR, proceed about 40km down Morice River FSR (driving past Aspen and Owen Lake Recreation Sites amongst others), the FSR turns to Morice Owen FSR, then turn right onto Morice Nadina FSR at about 60km, proceed on Morice Nadina FSR for about 15km where it turns into Huckleberry Mine FSR, stay on this mainline following signs for Twinkle Lake for about 20km. Access road will be on the left and is marked with a 3 blade sign.
